narrative.overview:
Every record is a document, drawn as a bill-of-lading form: a navy-ink outer rule, a grid of numbered boxed fields separated by pale blue form rules, small tracked caps for each caption. The user reads an invoice or a payment order the way they would read the paper original, then stamps it. Approval is not a badge or a toggle; it is a rotated violet stamp pressed onto the form, and a finished document carries its result as a large overprint across its head.

The surface is dense and calm. A navy top bar holds the module nav (Faturalar, Ödemeler) and the day's exchange rates; each module has its own paper subnav, and below it a ruled ledger lists records on the left and the selected document sits on the right. Nothing floats: there are no cards, no shadows, no rounded corners. Hierarchy comes from rules, weight and the single violet voice.

The world refuses the generic Bootstrap admin: cards, pill badges, soft shadows, and a sidebar duplicating the top nav.
keyCharacteristics: Records rendered as boxed, numbered form fields on off-white form paper.
Square corners everywhere; 1px rules, 1.5px ink outer rule on the form.
One accent, stamp violet, meaning approval and the single primary action.
Stamps and overprints are the only rotated, uppercase-heavy elements.
Tabular numerals for every amount, date and count; currency always printed beside the figure.

rules.name: The One Stamp Rule
rules.body: Violet means approval. It marks approved states, stamps, and exactly one primary action per screen; every other action is outlined ink. If two violet buttons appear on one screen, one is wrong.

rules.name: The No Amber Rule
rules.body: Pending has no hue of its own. Pending is navy ink text with an empty square marker, partway is navy ink with a half-filled square; the next approval slot is a solid 1.5px ink box, later slots are dashed rule-strong boxes.

rules.name: The Real Stamp Rule
rules.body: Stamp lettering (heavy, widely tracked caps) is reserved for real stamps and overprints that record a decision. Pending slots, statuses in lists and buttons use body type.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: Every amount, date, rate and count uses tabular numerals, and every amount prints its currency code beside it. Mixed currencies are listed side by side, never summed.

rules.name: The Ink Not Shadow Rule
rules.body: Nothing casts a shadow. Separation is a rule; emphasis is ink weight.

dos: Do draw every record as numbered boxed fields on form paper inside a 1.5px navy outer rule, ruled at 1px in form rule blue.
Do keep one violet primary action per screen; make every other action outlined ink.
Do show status with the four squares: empty (pending), half-filled (partway), filled (done), struck (rejected or cancelled); the next approval slot is a solid ink box, later slots dashed.
Do mark a finished document with the rotated, multiply-blended overprint across its head.
Do print every amount with tabular numerals and its currency code, in line-table captions too.
donts: Don't use rounded corners, cards, pill badges or shadows.
Don't introduce an amber or yellow pending colour.
Don't use stamp lettering for anything that is not a recorded decision.
Don't use violet decoratively or for a second action on the same screen.
Don't add a sidebar that repeats the top nav.
